questions.explanation: When a producer brings and sells a commodity in the market at a specified time, it is called supply and when a producer is ready to sell a commodity by bringing it to the market at a specified time and at a specified price, it is called a supply price. Generally the supply curve of a commodity is upward sloping to the right because in a given period of time more quantity of the commodity is produced and sold at a higher price because the producer is willing to sell more and more of the commodity at a higher price. Another important fact is that the marginal cost of producing additional units of output is increasing and the supply curve is upward sloping due to the possibility of maximum profit. And it is generally believed that the marginal cost of any firm is its supply curve above average variable cost.
questions.explanationEn: When a producer brings and sells a commodity in the market at a specified time, it is called supply and when a producer is ready to sell a commodity by bringing it to the market at a specified time and at a specified price, it is called a supply price. Another important fact is that the marginal cost of producing additional units of output is increasing and the supply curve is upward sloping due to the possibility of maximum profit. And it is generally believed that the marginal cost of any firm is its supply curve above average variable cost.

questions.questionText: National income is calculated by–
questions.questionTextEn: National income is calculated by–
options: at both prevailing and constant prices
optionsEn: at both prevailing and constant prices
questions.explanation: National income is calculated at both prevailing and constant prices. Under the calculation of national income current prices, the products of a given year are measured on the basis of the prices of the same year. Fluctuations in prices are included in this measure, due to which it does not measure the real national income. National income at constant prices is calculated by measuring the products of a given year at the prices of the base year. Base year prices as well as for other year thereafter. Therefore, it removes the fluctuations of prices, hence it expresses the real change in income. The economic growth of an economy is measured at constant prices.

questions.questionText: Who was the pioneer of green revolution in India?
questions.questionTextEn: Who was the pioneer of green revolution in India?
questions.explanation: Founder of green revolution in India, was M.S. Swaminathan. The green revolution in India started with the Kharif crop in 1966. HYVP was mainly limited to 5 crops wheat, paddy, sorghum, millet and maize but the maximum impact was felt in wheat. The green Revolution in India was the result of a combination of improved seeds, fertilizers and irrigation facilities. Its impact was visible in Punjab Haryana, western Uttar Pradesh and some districts of Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu.
